data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's claim asserts resumption is safe 'only if the system implements an atomic checkpoint,' but its own countercondition explicitly admits that event-sourced systems—where state is fully derivable from the event log alone—make checkpointing unnecessary. This makes the 'only if' claim false: there exists a legitimate, corruption-free resumption path that requires no checkpoint at all. The problem asks for 'precise conditions,' but SRC_001 over-restricts the necessary condition to one implementation mechanism (checkpoints) rather than identifying the true invariant (consistency between working state and committed log tail), which can be satisfied without checkpoints. The main claim is therefore not a precise statement of the resumption conditions.
